repeat: Set SCRATCH to a new folder with no sqlfluff config file above it, and REPO to the repository. The 'steps' of each input file have the commands that ran, with these names.

probe.research_code: yes: S3 research code, not sqll; no harness adapter or registry entry; no lint or fix command

build.build_time_note: Wall time of a release build with the crates fetched before (cargo fetch), 4 CPUs, on the build machine.

python_needed.generation: yes: utils/rustify.py imports sqlfluff (step 'generate the dialect tables', exit code 0)
python_needed.cargo_build: no: Python commands on PATH fail and record each call; 0 calls. sqlfluffrs_dialects/build.rs calls Python only if dialect/mod.rs is missing or older than a Python dialect or builder file.
python_needed.run: no: ldd and readelf show no libpython, and the probe runs in an image with no Python

generation.deterministic: utils/rustify.py check makes each file again and compares it with the file: exit code 0 with the installed sqlfluff 4.4.0 (PyPI) and with the src of the submodule

checks.parse_test: test_<dialect>_fixtures: the parse of each fixture with a .yml file gives no error. It does not compare the tree.
checks.yaml_shape_test: test_yaml_output_matches_python_<dialect>: the top-level keys and the child count of the root node are those of the .yml file. It does not compare the full tree. It stops at the first lex or parse error (a panic).

session.method: harness/bench.md: the CI image in docker, one container, serial, no network, no other load; the full profile; the tools run in turn for each repeat (timer.run_in_turn)
session.machine_lock: the command ran under flock /tmp/sqll-machine.lock (PROCESS.md, rule 7)

load.rule: start when the 1-minute load average is below 0.3; after the session, the 5-minute load average must be at most 1.5 (one serial process gives about 1)

notes: Each time is the median wall time of the timed runs of one benchmark (harness timer: process start to exit). Ratios: probe / other tool, on the same benchmark in the same session; below 1 means the probe is faster.

probe_over_sqlfluff uses the sqlfluff times of this session. baseline_over_session: the S2 baseline median (results/s2/baseline.json, another session) / the median of this session, for sqlfluff and sqruff; near 1 means the two sessions agree.

probe_phases: --timings of the probe, the median of 5 runs after the timed runs, in the same container. setup: the dialect and lexer setup (the lazy dialect tables); parse: root_parse; record: the sqlfluff record of the tree; write: the JSON output. The process start and exit are not in the phases.

generator.dialect_reader: rustify.py lists the dialects with sqlfluff.core.dialects.dialect_readout() and runs 3 builders for each dialect in a new Python process: build_dialect.py (mod.rs), build_lexers.py (matcher.rs), build_parsers.py --table-driven (parser.rs); build_dialects.py writes dialect/mod.rs. The builders load the dialect with dialect_selector(name). They read the Python objects: the dialect _library (each segment class and grammar), the lexer matchers (get_lexer_matchers), the bracket sets and reserved keywords (bracket_sets, sets), and the attributes of each grammar object.
generator.lines_note: table_builder_lines: the TableBuilder class of build_parsers.py (dialect reading, flattening, validation, and output). rust_emitter_lines: its generate_rust_tables method, the part that writes Rust.
generator.unknown_class_check: TableBuilder.validate() fails the generation if an instruction is 'Missing' (a grammar class with no handler).

facts.unhandled_grammar_classes: none: the generation passed TableBuilder.validate() for each dialect
facts.output_format: Rust statics of sqlfluffrs_types: GrammarTables (instructions, child ids, terminators, strings, aux data, hints, segment types and classes) for the parser; LexMatcher lists, keywords, and bracket pairs for the lexer

option3_reuse.conclusion: Option 3 can reuse the generator. It reads only the loaded Python dialect objects of the pinned sqlfluff, needs Python only to generate, gives the same output each time, and fails on a grammar class that it does not know. The sqlfluff dialects have no custom match code, so the tables hold the full grammar. Two ways: (a) keep the sqlfluffrs_types table format and write a new engine that reads it; (b) keep the table builder (dialect reading and flattening) and write a new emitter for another format. In both, the new engine must give the semantics that sqlfluffrs_parser gives to the tables (S4: exact trees). Risk: the generator reads private sqlfluff attributes, so a new sqlfluff version can break it; the pin limits this risk.
